   126	  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
   127	    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L)) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
   128	      hsub
   129	  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = Sheaf.h0 (P.gluedSheaf L) :=
   130	    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
   131	  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
   132	  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
   133	  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
   134	    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
   135	  exact_mod_cast hint

   137	/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/
   138	
   139	/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
   140	h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
   141	the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.
   142	
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
   144	`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
   145	`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
   146	fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
   147	`datumRigidEngine`. -/
   148	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
   149	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   150	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   151	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   152	    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   153	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   154	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   155	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   157	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   158	    [QuasiCompact
   159	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   160	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   162	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   163	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   164	    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   165	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
   166	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   167	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
   168	  haveI := hfin
   169	  haveI := hproj
   170	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
   171	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
   172	    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
   173	      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
   174	  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   175	      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   176	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   177	        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   178	    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   179	          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
   180	        (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
   181	    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
   182	    _ = 1 := hfibre

   184	/-! ## The certified-family specialization: N1 (invertible `H⁰`) and N3 (generators) -/
   185	
   186	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   187	/-- (Implementation) The fibre class of the divisor datum has `classDeg = n` at `κ(p)`:
   188	the base change of `G.eqns`, read through `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`. -/
   189	private theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum
   190	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   191	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   193	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   194	    [QuasiCompact
   195	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   196	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   197	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   198	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   199	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)] :
   200	    classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   201	      (G.adaptation.divisorDatum.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ) := by
   202	  have hcl : G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = (DivFam.mk G).toZar.picClass := by
   203	    rw [G.adaptation.cechPicClass_divisorDatum, DivFamZar.picClass_toZar, DivFam.picClass_mk]
   204	  rw [G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField, hcl,
   205	    ← DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg]
   206	  exact DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass
   207	    (DivFamZar.mapAlg p.asIdeal.ResidueField n (DivFam.mk G).toZar)
   208	
   209	/-- **N1 — invertibility of the canonical `H⁰`** (worksheet §2 (N1)): for a certified
   210	divisor family `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus `V` (`hvan`), the divisor datum
   211	`D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has `H⁰` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at every prime.
   212	
   213	The fibre-degree hypothesis of `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is discharged uniformly:
   214	the fibre class of `D_G` at `κ(p)` is the base change of `G.eqns`, which has
   215	`classDeg = n` at every field (`DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`). -/
   216	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one
   217	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   218	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   219	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   220	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   221	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   222	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   223	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   224	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   225	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   226	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   227	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   228	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   229	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   230	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   231	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   232	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   233	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   234	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   235	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   236	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   237	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   238	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   239	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   240	  exact G.adaptation.divisorDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one hπ hχ hfib p
   241	    (G.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum p)
   242	
   243	/-- **N3 — the generator kit** (worksheet §2 (N3)): since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of
   244	stalk-rank `1` on the locus, its `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial, so a fibrewise-nonzero
   245	**global** section exists on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` — the Zariski-local generator
   246	(`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood kit of
   247	`Picard/LocalGenerators.lean`). -/
   248	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum
   249	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   250	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   251	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   252	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   253	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   254	    ∃ f : S, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0,
   255	      ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum S, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
   256	        (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   257	            Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
   258	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   259	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   260	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   261	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine G.adaptation.divisorDatum hπ hfib
   262	  haveI := hfin
   263	  haveI := hproj
   264	  have hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   265	    G.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one hπ hχ hvan p
   266	  -- rank 1 ⟹ the `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial
   267	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   268	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) = 1 := by
   269	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]; exact hrank
   270	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S]
   271	      Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) :=
   272	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   273	  have hnt : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S]
   274	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   275	    (TensorProduct.comm S _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   276	  exact Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p hnt

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-C C0 — the datum inverse, the divisor datum, and the canonical section
    11	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-1 + §2 (N2))
    12	
    13	Every landed datum built from a divisor family is the *twisted ideal* datum
    14	`𝒪(Θᵃ − d)` of class `θᵃ·[d]⁻¹` (G-0a). DAT-C's normalization layer needs a datum in
    15	the class `[𝒪(d)]` itself, together with its canonical section. This file pins both:
    16	
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.inv` — the **datum inverse**: same cover
    18	  data, transition units `(g i j)⁻¹`; the cocycle law inverts termwise.
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_inv` — the class law
    20	  `D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹` (subordinated-cocycle level).
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relThetaCocycle_zero`, `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero`,
    22	  `thetaChartUnit_zero`, `cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero` — at exponent `a = 0`
    23	  the theta twisting cocycle is trivial, so the whole-chart theta datum has class `1`
    24	  **over an arbitrary test ring** (the worksheet cites the base-`k` class law
    25	  `cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum` + `fiberTwist_zero`; the direct `a = 0` computation
    26	  is ring-generic, which the §2 consumers need — recorded deviation).
    27	* `DivisorAdaptation.divisorDatum` — **the divisor datum**
    28	  `(A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv`, with class law
    29	  `cechPicClass_divisorDatum : A.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = d.picClass`
    30	  (G-0a at `a = 0` + the trivial theta block + `cechPicClass_inv`).
    31	* `DivisorAdaptation.canonSection` — **the canonical section is the equation system
    32	  itself** (N2): the components `(A.eqn j)` satisfy the inverse-datum matching
    33	  condition (`eqn_mul_eqnRatio` read against the inverted units), giving a global
    34	  section of the divisor datum's glued sheaf.
    35	* `DivisorAdaptation.divEq_sectionLocalEquations_canonSection` — **(N2) cut-back by
    36	  pure refinement**: the `LocalEquations` datum cut by `canonSection` (DAT-A
    37	  `sectionLocalEquations`, on any subordinated pointed cover) is `DivEq` to `d` —
    38	  the comparison units are the adaptation's own `eqn_rel` units; no fibre argument.
    39	-/

    63	/-- The pair value of an inverse unit cocycle is the inverse pair value. -/
    64	private lemma inv_unitsEvInf {X : Scheme.{u}} {𝒰 : X.PointedCover}
    65	    (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j : X) :
    66	    Scheme.unitsEvInf γ⁻¹ i j = (Scheme.unitsEvInf γ i j)⁻¹ := rfl
    67	
    68	/-- The unit-level cocycle identity of a datum (the value-level law `mul_res`
    69	re-packaged through `Units.ext`). -/
    70	private lemma unitsRestrict_unit_mul (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    71	    (i j l : D.index) :
    72	    (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict
    73	        (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces l ≤ D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
    74	        (D.unit i j)
    75	      * (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclCoc D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
    76	          (D.unit j l)
    77	      = (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
    78	          (D.unit i l) :=
    79	  Units.ext (D.isGluingCocycle.mul_res i j l)
    80	
    81	/-- **The datum inverse** (worksheet GAP-1): the same basic-open cover data with the
    82	termwise-inverted transition units `(g i j)⁻¹`. The cocycle law inverts termwise —
    83	the units are honest `Units`, and the section rings are commutative. -/
    84	noncomputable def inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
    85	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π where
    86	  toBasicOpenCoverData := D.toBasicOpenCoverData
    87	  unit i j := (D.unit i j)⁻¹
    88	  isGluingCocycle := by
    89	    constructor
    90	    · intro i
    91	      rw [show D.unit i i = 1 from Units.ext (D.isGluingCocycle.unit_self i), inv_one,
    92	        Units.val_one]
    93	    · intro i j l
    94	      have key : ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict
    95	            (inf_le_left :
    96	              D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces l ≤ D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
    97	            (D.unit i j))⁻¹
    98	          * ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclCoc D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
    99	              (D.unit j l))⁻¹
   100	          = ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
   101	              (D.unit i l))⁻¹ := by
   102	        rw [← mul_inv]
   103	        exact congrArg (·⁻¹) (D.unitsRestrict_unit_mul i j l)
   104	      have hval := congrArg Units.val key
   105	      rw [Units.val_mul] at hval
   106	      exact hval
   107

   113	    D.inv.unit i j = (D.unit i j)⁻¹ := rfl

   115	/-- **The class law of the datum inverse**: `[D⁻¹] = [D]⁻¹`. Both classes are computed
   116	by subordinated cocycles on `D`'s canonical pointed cover by pieces, where the
   117	subordinated cocycle of the inverse datum is the inverse cocycle. -/
   118	theorem cechPicClass_inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
   119	    D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := by
   120	  have hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B,
   121	      D.pointedCover.opens x ≤ D.inv.pieces (D.pieceIndex x) :=
   122	    fun _ => le_rfl
   123	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ
   124	      = (gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   125	          (fun _ => le_rfl))⁻¹ := by
   126	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
   127	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, inv_unitsEvInf, gluedSubordCocycle_evInf]
   128	    exact Units.ext rfl
   129	  calc D.inv.cechPicClass
   130	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
   131	          (gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   132	            hσ).class :=
   133	        (D.inv.cechPicClass_eq_mk D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ).symm
   134	    _ = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
   135	          ((gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   136	            (fun _ => le_rfl)).class)⁻¹ := by
   137	        rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_inv]
   138	    _ = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := rfl

   142	/-! ## The theta block is trivial at exponent zero -/

   148	/-- The relative theta cocycle at exponent `0` is the trivial unit: `t₀⁰ = 1`. -/
   149	theorem relThetaCocycle_zero : relThetaCocycle C B π 0 = 1 := by
   150	  change relUnitCocycle C B (fiberTwoCover π) (thetaUnit π ^ 0) = 1
   151	  rw [pow_zero]
   152	  exact map_one _
   153	
   154	/-- The theta twisting units of a finite cover datum are trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   155	theorem FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero (D : FinCoverData C B π) (i j : D.index) :
   156	    D.thetaOvlUnit 0 i j = 1 := by
   157	  rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   158	  · rfl
   159	  · rw [FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inl_inr, relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   160	  · rw [FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inr_inl, relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one, inv_one]
   161	  · rfl
   162	
   163	/-- The whole-chart theta transition units are trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   164	theorem thetaChartUnit_zero (i j : (thetaChartCover C B π).index) :
   165	    thetaChartUnit C B π 0 i j = 1 := by
   166	  rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   167	  · rfl
   168	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0) = 1
   169	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   170	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0)⁻¹ = 1
   171	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, inv_one, map_one]
   172	  · rfl

   174	/-- **The whole-chart theta datum has trivial class at exponent `0`, over an arbitrary
   175	test ring**: all its transition units are `1`, so the subordinated cocycle is the
   176	trivial cocycle. (Ring-generic strengthening of the base-`k` route
   177	`cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum` + `fiberTwist_zero`.) -/
   178	theorem cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero :
   179	    (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).cechPicClass = 1 := by
   180	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).isGluingCocycle
   181	      (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex
   182	      (fun _ => le_rfl) = 1 := by
   183	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
   184	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, Scheme.one_unitsEvInf]
   185	    change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _
   186	        (thetaChartUnit C B π 0 ((thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex x)
   187	          ((thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex y)) = 1
   188	    rw [thetaChartUnit_zero, map_one]
   189	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover
   190	      (gluedSubordCocycle (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).isGluingCocycle
   191	        (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex
   192	        (fun _ => le_rfl)).class = 1
   193	  rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_one, Scheme.CechPic.mk_one]

   197	/-! ## The divisor datum and its class law -/
   198	
   199	namespace DivisorAdaptation
   200	
   201	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   202	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   203	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
   204	
   205	/-- The ideal transition units at exponent `0` are the plain ratio units `f_j/f_i`:
   206	the theta block is trivial. -/
   207	theorem thetaIdealUnit_zero (i j : A.index) :
   208	    A.thetaIdealUnit 0 i j = A.eqnRatio i j := by
   209	  rw [thetaIdealUnit, A.toFinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero, mul_one]
   210	
   211	/-- **The divisor datum of an adaptation** (worksheet GAP-1): the inverse of the
   212	twisted ideal datum at exponent `0` — a pinned cocycle datum in the class `[𝒪(d)]`
   213	(`cechPicClass_divisorDatum`), whose transition units are the inverted ratio units
   214	`(f_j/f_i)⁻¹`. -/
   215	noncomputable def divisorDatum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R π :=
   216	  (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv
   217	
   218	/-- **The class law of the divisor datum**: `[divisorDatum] = [𝒪(d)]` — G-0a at
   219	`a = 0`, the trivial theta block, and the class law of the datum inverse. -/
   220	theorem cechPicClass_divisorDatum : A.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = d.picClass := by
   221	  change (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv.cechPicClass = d.picClass
   222	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_inv, A.cechPicClass_thetaIdealDatum 0,
   223	    cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero, one_mul, inv_inv]
   224	
   225	/-! ### The canonical section -/
   226	
   227	/-- The value-level matching law of the equation components against the inverted ratio
   228	units: `f_i = (f_j/f_i)⁻¹ · f_j` on any open below the piece overlap. -/
   229	private lemma res_eqn_eq_inv_eqnRatio_mul (i j : A.index) {O : (relCurve C R).Opens}
   230	    (hO : O ≤ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :
   231	    (relCurve C R).resHom (hO.trans inf_le_left) (A.eqn i)
   232	      = (relCurve C R).resHom hO
   233	          (((A.eqnRatio i j)⁻¹ : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ) :
   234	            Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j))
   235	        * (relCurve C R).resHom (hO.trans inf_le_right) (A.eqn j) := by
   236	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hO) (A.eqn_mul_eqnRatio i j)
   237	  rw [map_mul] at key
   238	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
   239	  -- key : `res f_i · res (f_j/f_i) = res f_j` on `O`; divide by the restricted unit
   240	  refine (Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq
   241	    ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hO (A.eqnRatio i j))).mpr ?_
   242	  rw [mul_comm]
   243	  exact key
   244	
   245	/-- The matching condition of the equation components for the divisor datum, in the
   246	exact shape of the `gluedSubmodule` carrier at `W = ⊤` (adaptation-index form; each
   247	datum-index case is definitionally this statement). -/
   248	private lemma canon_matching (i j : A.index) :
   249	    (relCurve C R).resHom
   250	        (inf_le_left : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i)
   251	        ((relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))
   252	      = (relCurve C R).resHom
   253	          (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right :
   254	            ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)
   255	          (((A.thetaIdealUnit 0 i j)⁻¹ :
   256	              Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ) :
   257	            Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j))
   258	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
   259	            (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
   260	              ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces j)
   261	            ((relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j)
   262	              (A.eqn j)) := by
   263	  rw [A.thetaIdealUnit_zero i j]
   264	  have key := A.res_eqn_eq_inv_eqnRatio_mul i j
   265	    (O := ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)
   266	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right)
   267	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
   268	  exact key
   269	
   270	/-- **The canonical section of the divisor datum is the equation system itself**
   271	(worksheet §2 (N2)): the components `A.eqn j`, restricted to the pieces, form a
   272	matching family for the inverted ratio units — a global section of the divisor
   273	datum's glued sheaf. -/
   274	noncomputable def canonSection :
   275	    ↥(_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSubmodule R A.divisorDatum.pieces
   276	        A.divisorDatum.unit ⊤) :=
   277	  ⟨fun j => (relCurve C R).resHom
   278	      (inf_le_right.trans (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j)))
   279	      (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)),
   280	    by
   281	      intro i j
   282	      rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   283	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inl i.down) (Sum.inl j.down)
   284	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inl i.down) (Sum.inr j.down)
   285	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inr i.down) (Sum.inl j.down)
   286	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inr i.down) (Sum.inr j.down)⟩
   287	
   288	/-- The components of the canonical section are the (piece-restricted) equations. -/
   289	lemma component_canonSection (j : (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index) :
   290	    A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j
   291	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j))
   292	          (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) :=
   293	  Scheme.resHom_resHom _ _ _
   294	
   295	/-- The canonical section is germ-regular: its components are the adaptation's own
   296	regular equations (`eqn_regular`) — the `hreg` input of `sectionLocalEquations`,
   297	with no fibrewise hypothesis. -/
   298	theorem germ_component_canonSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   299	    (j : (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index) (y : relCurve C R)
   300	    (hy : y ∈ A.divisorDatum.pieces j) :
   301	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.divisorDatum.pieces j) y hy).hom
   302	        (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j)
   303	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
   304	  have hy' : y ∈ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 j) :=
   305	    (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j)) hy
   306	  have hswap : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.divisorDatum.pieces j) y hy).hom
   307	      (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j)
   308	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) y hy').hom
   309	          (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) := by
   310	    rw [A.component_canonSection j]
   311	    exact TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _
   312	  rw [hswap]
   313	  exact A.eqn_regular (A.lowerIndex 0 j) y hy'
   314	
   315	/-- **(N2) — the canonical section cuts back `d` by pure refinement**: the
   316	`LocalEquations` datum cut by the canonical section on any pointed cover subordinated
   317	to the pieces is `DivEq` to `d`. The common refinement is `𝒲 ⊓ d.cover`, and the
   318	comparison units are the adaptation's own `eqn_rel` units (`relUnit`) — no fibre
   319	argument anywhere. -/
   320	theorem divEq_sectionLocalEquations_canonSection
   321	    (𝒲 : (relCurve C R).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C R → (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index)
   322	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C R, 𝒲.opens y ≤ A.divisorDatum.pieces (σ y)) :
   323	    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
   324	      (A.divisorDatum.sectionLocalEquations A.canonSection 𝒲 σ hσ
   325	        (fun j y hy => A.germ_component_canonSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors j y hy))
   326	      d := by
   327	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ d.cover, fun x => inf_le_left, fun x => inf_le_right, fun x => ?_⟩
   328	  -- the piece through `x` sits inside the adaptation piece of its lowered index
   329	  have hpc : 𝒲.opens x ≤ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) :=
   330	    (hσ x).trans (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 (σ x)))
   331	  have hle : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x
   332	      ≤ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) ⊓ d.cover.opens x :=
   333	    inf_le_inf_right _ hpc
   334	  refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hle (A.relUnit (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) x), ?_⟩
   335	  -- the defining equation of the comparison unit, restricted to the refinement
   336	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hle)
   337	    (A.res_eqn_eq_relUnit_mul (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) x)
   338	  rw [map_mul] at key
   339	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
   340	  -- collapse the constructed datum's restricted equation onto the adaptation
   341	  -- equation, term-mode (`rw` walks into the relCurve spelling seam — I-0237(a))
   342	  have hlhs := (Scheme.resHom_resHom (hσ x)
   343	      (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)
   344	      (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection (σ x))).trans
   345	    ((congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
   346	        ((inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x).trans (hσ x)))
   347	      (A.component_canonSection (σ x))).trans
   348	      (Scheme.resHom_resHom (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 (σ x)))
   349	        ((inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x).trans (hσ x))
   350	        (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)))))
   351	  exact hlhs.trans key
   352	
   353	end DivisorAdaptation

    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/

    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.

    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf

   227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
   228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
   229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
   230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
   231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
   232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
   233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where

     9	/-!
    10	# Restricting a scheme module to the base ring
    11	
    12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, this file views an `X.Modules` object as a sheaf of
    13	`k`-modules.  The construction keeps the same section types and restriction maps; only the
    14	scalar action is restricted along `k -> Gamma(X, U)`.  It is the dialect bridge needed to
    15	compare a `Scheme.Modules` line bundle with the fixed-base module sheaves used by the Cech
    16	cohomology engine.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    26	
    27	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
    28	
    29	/-- The base-ring module structure on sections of a scheme module. -/
    30	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleKSections
    31	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    32	    (U : X.left.Opens) : Module k Γ(M, U) :=
    33	  Module.compHom _ (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U)
    34	
    35	attribute [local instance] moduleKSections
    36	
    37	/-- The native structure-sheaf action, with section-notation binders kept explicit. -/
    38	private noncomputable def smulSection
    39	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    40	    (U : X.left.Opens) (r : Γ(X.left, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : Γ(M, U) :=
    41	  r • x
    42	
    43	/-- The presheaf underlying a scheme module after restriction of scalars to the base ring. -/
    44	noncomputable def toModuleKPresheafOfModules
    45	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    46	    X.left.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
    47	  obj U := ModuleCat.of k Γ(M, U.unop)
    48	  map {U V} f := ModuleCat.ofHom
    49	    { toFun := fun x => M.presheaf.map f x
    50	      map_add' := fun x y => map_add _ x y
    51	      map_smul' := fun r x =>
    52	        (Scheme.Modules.map_smul M f.unop (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U.unop r) x).trans
    53	          (congrArg
    54	            (fun (s : Γ(X.left, V.unop)) =>
    55	              smulSection X M V.unop s (M.presheaf.map f x))
    56	            (X.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k f r)) }
    57	  map_id U := by
    58	    ext x
    59	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (f : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj U) =>
    60	      (ConcreteCategory.hom f : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_id U)) x
    61	  map_comp {U V W} f g := by
    62	    ext x
    63	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (h : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj W) =>
    64	      (ConcreteCategory.hom h : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_comp f g)) x
    65	
    66	/-- The restricted presheaf is a sheaf because its underlying additive presheaf is unchanged. -/
    67	lemma toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf
    68	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    69	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat)

    11	/-!
    12	# Chart-module structure of the m-chart glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1c)
    13	
    14	The `Γ(X, V)`-module and coefficient-ring properties of the glued section module
    15	`F(V)` on an affine chart `V` carrying a finite subordinate trivializing basic-open
    16	family (`informal/spec-dat-1.md`, decision (D5)): sections `h : ι → Γ(X, V)` whose
    17	basic opens `D(h i)` lie in gluing pieces (`hP : D(h i) ≤ U (σ i)`) and span the unit
    18	ideal (`hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤` — the worksheet partition witness feeds
    19	this through `Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one`).
    20	
    21	All statements are relative to an ambient packaging
    22	`[Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V]` whose action is componentwise (the hypothesis
    23	`hq`, discharged by `rfl` for packagings built by `gluedQcohOn` — the same interface as
    24	`gluedPairData`), with the chart module structure `Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE` bound by
    25	`letI` in statements (RE-0 pattern) and the section modules in the sheaf-object
    26	spelling `(gluedSheaf k U g).obj.obj (op W)` — the spelling the engine consumes.
    27	
    28	* `gluedPieceModule`/`gluedPieceEquiv` — each piece `F(D(h i))` is a free rank-one
    29	  `Γ(X, D(h i))`-module through the piece trivialization `gluedTriv`;
    30	* `isUnit_algebraMap_end_glued` — a chart section restricting to a unit acts invertibly
    31	  on the glued sections of an open below a piece (trivialization conjugation);
    32	* `isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued` — **the RE-0 bridge fired per piece**:
    33	  `F(V) → F(D(h i))` is an `IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (h i))` (the abstract
    34	  bridge at `V ⊓ D(h i)`, transported across the opens equality `V ⊓ D(h i) = D(h i)`
    35	  by `IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv`);
    36	* the localization-local chart properties: `moduleFinite_glued`,
    37	  `finitePresentation_glued`, `flat_glued`, `projective_glued` (over `Γ(X, V)`), and
    38	  the coefficient-ring transports `flat_glued_of_flat` (under `Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)` —

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.PullbackContinuous
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Presheaf
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.OpenImmersion

/-!
# The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme

In this file, we define the abelian category of sheaves of modules
`X.Modules` over a scheme `X`, and study its basic functoriality.

-/

@[expose] public section

universe t u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace SheafOfModules Bicategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

variable {X Y Z T : Scheme.{u}}

variable (X) in
/-- The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme. -/
def Modules := SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf

namespace Modules

/-- Morphisms between `𝒪ₓ`-modules. Use `Hom.app` to act on sections. -/
def Hom (M N : X.Modules) : Type u := SheafOfModules.Hom M N

instance : Category X.Modules where
  Hom := Modules.Hom
  __ := (inferInstance : Category (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))

noncomputable instance : Abelian X.Modules :=
  inferInstanceAs <| Abelian (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
instance : HasLimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasLimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))
instance : HasColimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasColimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))

section Functor

variable (X) in
/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules.
This is mostly useful to transport results from (pre)sheaves of modules to `𝒪ₓ`-modules and
usually shouldn't be used directly when working with actual `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
def toPresheafOfModules : X.Modules ⥤ X.PresheafOfModules := SheafOfModules.forget _

/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules is fully faithful. -/
def fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules : (Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).FullyFaithful :=
  SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _

instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Full := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.full
instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Faithful := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.faithful
instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).IsRightAdjoint :=
  (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).isRightAdjoint

variable (X) in
/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of abelian groups. -/
noncomputable def toPresheaf : X.Modules ⥤ TopCat.Presheaf Ab X :=
  toPresheafOfModules X ⋙ PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _

instance : (toPresheaf X).Faithful := .comp _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)
instance : PreservesLimits (toPresheaf X) := comp_preservesLimits _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)
instance : (toPresheaf X).ReflectsIsomorphisms :=
  reflectsIsomorphisms_comp _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)

end Functor

variable {M N K : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N} {U V : X.Opens}

section Presheaf

/-- The underlying abelian presheaf of an `𝒪ₓ`-module. -/
noncomputable def presheaf (M : X.Modules) : TopCat.Presheaf Ab X := M.1.presheaf

/-- Notation for sections of a presheaf of module. -/
scoped[AlgebraicGeometry] notation3 "Γ(" M ", " U ")" => (Scheme.Modules.presheaf M).obj (.op U)

instance : Module Γ(X, U) Γ(M, U) := (M.val.obj (.op U)).isModule

variable (M) in
@[simp] lemma map_smul (i : U ⟶ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (x : Γ(M, V)) :
    M.presheaf.map i.op (r • x) = X.presheaf.map i.op r • M.presheaf.map i.op x :=
  M.val.map_smul _ _ _

/-- Scalar multiplication as an endomorphism of `Γ(M, U)`. -/
def smul : Γ(X, U) →+* End Γ(M, U) :=
  (M.val.obj (.op U)).smul

@[simp]
lemma smul_apply (r : Γ(X, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : (M.smul r).hom x = r • x := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma map_comp_smul (i : U ⟶ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) :
    M.smul r ≫ M.presheaf.map i.op = M.presheaf.map i.op ≫ M.smul (X.presheaf.map i.op r) := by
  ext
  simp

/-- The underlying map between abelian presheaves of a morphism of `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
noncomputable def Hom.mapPresheaf (φ : M ⟶ N) : M.presheaf ⟶ N.presheaf :=
  (toPresheaf X).map φ

/-- The application of a morphism of `𝒪ₓ`-modules to sections. -/
def Hom.app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U : X.Opens) : Γ(M, U) ⟶ Γ(N, U) :=
  (forget₂ _ _).map (φ.val.app (.op U))

@[simp] lemma mapPresheaf_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U) : φ.mapPresheaf.app U = φ.app U.unop := rfl

@[simp]
lemma Hom.app_smul (φ : M ⟶ N) (r : Γ(X, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) :
    φ.app U (r • x) = r • φ.app U x :=
  (φ.val.app (.op U)).hom.map_smul r x

@[simp] lemma Hom.add_app (φ ψ : M ⟶ N) : (φ + ψ).app U = φ.app U + ψ.app U := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.sub_app (φ ψ : M ⟶ N) : (φ - ψ).app U = φ.app U - ψ.app U := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.zero_app : (0 : M ⟶ N).app U = 0 := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.id_app (M : X.Modules) : (𝟙 M :).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.comp_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (ψ : N ⟶ K) : (φ ≫ ψ).app U = φ.app U ≫ ψ.app U := rfl

@[ext]
lemma hom_ext (f g : M ⟶ N) (H : ∀ U, f.app U = g.app U) : f = g := by
  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
  ext U x
  exact congr($(H U.unop) x)

lemma isSheaf (M : X.Modules) : M.presheaf.IsSheaf := SheafOfModules.isSheaf M

@[simp] lemma toPresheaf_obj : (toPresheaf X).obj M = M.presheaf := rfl
@[simp] lemma toPresheaf_map : (toPresheaf X).map φ = φ.mapPresheaf := rfl

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app {M N : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N} :
    IsIso φ ↔ ∀ U, IsIso (φ.app U) := by
  rw [← isIso_iff_of_reflects_iso _ (toPresheaf X), NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app]
  simp [Opposite.op_surjective.forall]

instance [IsIso φ] : IsIso (φ.app U) := Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app.mp ‹_› _

@[simp, push ←]
lemma inv_app [IsIso φ] : (inv φ).app U = inv (φ.app U) := by
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_hom_inv_id
  simp [← Hom.comp_app]

end Presheaf

lemma pushforward_obj_obj (M : X.Modules) (U : Y.Opens) :

    11	# W6-full: the glued sheaf of a meromorphic presentation is the divisor sheaf (DAT-3 (c))
    12	
    13	For the curve bundle `X` — integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact
    14	over a field `K` — and a meromorphic presentation `P` (`Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation`:
    15	a pointed cover, a unit cocycle on it, and trivializing elements `P.elem x ∈ K(X)ˣ` whose
    16	ratios are the germs at `η` of the cocycle values), this file identifies the m-chart
    17	cocycle-glued sheaf of `P` with the divisor sheaf of its presentation divisor — the core
    18	of the W6-full seam (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §3.1(c), spec FROZEN there):
    19	
    20	* `Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.isGluingCocycle` — the presentation's cocycle satisfies
    21	  the gluing cocycle law (`unit_self` from the ratio property at `(x, x)` through the
    22	  injective germ embedding; `mul_res` is the landed `unitsEvInf_trans`);
    23	* `Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.gluedSheaf` — the glued sheaf of `K`-modules of the
    24	  presentation, `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSheaf` on `P.cover.opens` with multipliers the
    25	  pair values of `P.cocycle`;
    26	* `Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.gluedDivisorSheafIso` —
    27	  **`glued(P) ≅ 𝒪(presentationDivisor P)`**: over a nonempty open the components send a
    28	  matching family `s` to the rational function `(P.elem x)⁻¹ · germ_η (s x)` (independent
    29	  of the piece `x` — `gluedVal_eq_elem_inv_mul`); the inverse trivializes a bounded
    30	  rational function `h` chartwise as the section with germ `P.elem x · h` (the
    31	  `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` mechanism, chartwise, through the `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X` gluing engine
    32	  `exists_section_germ_eq`).
    33	
    34	## The pole-bound bridge
    35	
    36	At a closed point `z` of a piece, the divisor bound of `presentationDivisor K P` is the
    37	coerced order `ordZ_z (P.elem z)` (`divisorBound_presentationDivisor`), and every piece
    38	element `P.elem x` with `z` in its piece has the same order (`ordZ_elem_eq`). So
    39	multiplication by `P.elem x` converts the pole bound `D` into the pole bound `0` exactly,
    40	and integrality glues to honest sections by the landed `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X` machinery.
    41	
    42	The `Subsingleton`/`h⁰`/FLV consequences (the `hfib` sheaf-form discharge and the rank
    43	export) are assembled in `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.W6Full`.

   697	/-- The cocycle datum tied to a genus-degree presentation has class degree `genus C`
   698	after every field-valued coefficient extension.
   699	
   700	The proof follows the presentation itself: restrict `lam` to its etale-cover carrier,
   701	identify that class with `representative`, rewrite it as the datum's relative Picard class,
   702	and read the defining degree condition of `lam`. -/
   703	theorem datum_classDeg_baseChange
   704	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   705	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier L]
   706	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier L] :
   707	    classDeg L
   708	      (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   709	        P.datum.cechPicClass) = genus C := by
   710	  let iota : A →ₐ[k] P.cover.Carrier :=
   711	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k
   712	  let psi : P.cover.Carrier →ₐ[k] L :=
   713	    (Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier L).restrictScalars k
   714	  have hcurve :
   715	      relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L =
   716	        (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap psi).left := by
   717	    refine congrArg
   718	      (fun f : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k P.cover.Carrier => (C ◁ f).left) ?_
   719	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   720	  have hpresentation :
   721	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 =
   722	        relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   723	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) := by
   724	    exact picEtMap_eq_relPicToPicEt_of_affineRepresentative
   725	      C lam.1 P.cover P.representative P.represents.symm

   727	    classDeg L
   728	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   729	          P.datum.cechPicClass) =
   730	      relPicDeg L
   731	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
   732	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   733	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) :=
   734	      (relPicDeg_relPicMk L _).symm
   735	    _ = relPicDeg L
   736	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   737	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   738	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) := by
   739	      rw [relPicMap_mk, ← hcurve]
   740	      rfl
   741	    _ = relPicDeg L
   742	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   743	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) := by
   744	      rw [P.datum_class]
   745	    _ = degAt
   746	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   747	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)))
   748	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) :=
   749	      (degAt_relPicToPicEt
   750	        (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))
   751	        (Over.overSpecMap psi)).symm
   752	    _ = degAt (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1)
   753	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) := by rw [hpresentation]
   754	    _ = degAt lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) :=
   755	      degAt_picEtMap (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   756	    _ = genus C := lam.2 L (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota)
   757

     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    21	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    60	
    61	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    62	
    63	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    64	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    65	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    66	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    67	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    68	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    69	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    70	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    71	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    72	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    73	
    74	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    75	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    76	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    77	contract. -/
    78	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    79	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    80	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    81	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    82	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    83	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    84	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    88	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    89	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    90	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    91	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    92	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    93	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    94	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    95	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    96	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    97	
    98	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
    99	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   100	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   101	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   102	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   103	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   104	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
   105	
   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   108	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   110	
   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   112	
   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/
   116	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   118	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   119	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   120	
   121	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   122	
   123	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   124	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   125	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   126	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   127	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
   128	
   129	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   130	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   131	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   132	  h
   133	
   134	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   135	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   136	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   137	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   138	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   139	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   140	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   141	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   142	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   143	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   144	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   145	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   146	  h.property g fst snd hpb
   147	
   148	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   149	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   150	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   151	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   152	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   153	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   154	
   155	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   156	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   157	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   158	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   159	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   160	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h
   161	
   162	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   163	
   164	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
   165	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
   166	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
   167	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
   168	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   169	
   170	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
   171	representer. -/
   172	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   173	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
   174	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
   175	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   176	
   177	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   178	def rankOneAbelAff :
   179	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
   180	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   181	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   182	
   183	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   184	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   185	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   186	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   187	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   188	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   189	
   190	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   191	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   192	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   193	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   194	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi
   195	
   196	/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
   197	The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this
   198	theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
   199	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   200	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
   201	    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
   202	      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
   203	  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property
   204	
   205	end
   206	
   207	end AlgebraicGeometry
